caption: Examples of the network input: square crops inscribed in the circular ROI, albumin and creatinine assays, four random tests per class. Differences between classes are subtle and are not obvious to the eye.

Strategy A (frozen embeddings): (a) mean macro-F1 using the albumin crop only, the creatinine crop only, or both, compared with the hand-crafted reference (dashed black) and the baselines (red); (b) fold-wise macro-F1 with both assays.

Unsupervised PCA of the frozen mobilenet_v3_large embeddings coloured by (a) class, (b) illumination and (c) sample. Spearman correlation of PC1/PC2 with lux: 0.30 / 0.19. Tight clusters in (c) show that repeats of one sample resemble each other more than they resemble their class — the reason for grouped validation.

Measurement audit with CNN embeddings: cross-validated R² for log albumin (albumin crop), log creatinine (creatinine crop), log UACR (both) and lux (both). Grey bars = hand-crafted features (Path A). CNN features do not break the information limit if their bars are not clearly higher than the grey ones.
All models on the identical outer folds: (a) fold-wise macro-F1 (dots = folds; colour = model family), (b) mean of five metrics, (c) mean recall per class. The MICRO column is the critical one.
Pooled out-of-fold confusion matrices (repeat 1, test level; counts and row-normalised percentage) of the best CNN-based models and of the reference classical model.

Learning curves averaged over the outer folds: (a) training loss; (b) test log-loss and (c) test macro-F1 after every epoch. The test curves are a diagnostic only — they were never used to choose the epoch, the learning rate or the model.

Grad-CAM of the selected fine-tuned model (efficientnet_b0 (fine-tuned)) for random held-out tests of each class (rows: NORMAL, MICRO, MACRO). Warm colours = regions that raise the score of the predicted class. Left of each pair: crop; right: overlay.
Effect of input perturbations on the macro-F1 of the selected CNN (single held-out fold, ≈ 95 tests; indicative only).
